blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Small talk is a very British habit. Before any real conversation, British people often say a few light, safe comments — about the weather, the weekend, the traffic or the football.

It looks simple, but it matters. Small talk is how the British show they are friendly without getting too personal too fast. A good small-talker uses question tags often: "Lovely day, isn't it?" or "Terrible traffic, wasn't there?"

When in doubt, start with the weather. You will almost always be right.

items.q: What do British people often talk about before a real conversation?
options: The weather, the weekend or the traffic
items.why: "about the weather, the weekend, the traffic or the football" — são os assuntos leves do small talk.

items.q: Why do the British use small talk?
options: To show they are friendly without getting too personal
items.why: "how the British show they are friendly without getting too personal too fast."

items.q: What does a good small-talker use often?
items.why: "A good small-talker uses question tags often."

items.q: The text suggests that the weather is…
options: a safe topic that almost always works
items.why: Inferência: "start with the weather. You will almost always be right." — é um tema seguro.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: Small talk is friendly and safe.
The weather is a good way to start.
You should ask about money and age first.
items.why: Inferência: o texto valoriza temas leves e seguros; perguntar sobre dinheiro e idade é o oposto.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily ajudando a nova colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi! Welcome to the London office. Let me help you before your first meeting.

Here, we do a little small talk first. It is normal. For two or three minutes, people just chat. Nobody starts with business right away. It is our way to be friendly.

Start with the weather. It is always safe. You can say, "Lovely day, isn't it?" or "Cold this morning, isn't it?" People love that. You can also ask about the weekend. Just say, "Good weekend?" and smile.

One tip: use question tags. They are short and friendly. "Nice coffee, isn't it?" Try it. It sounds very British.

But please, no personal questions. Do not ask about money, age or salary. That is not polite here.

So relax, smile, and talk about the weather. You will be fine. Ready? Let's go in.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What do people do first in the London office?
options: A little small talk for two or three minutes
items.why: "For two or three minutes, people just chat."

items.q: What topic does Emily say is always safe?
items.why: "Start with the weather. It is always safe."

items.q: Which question tag does Emily use as an example?
items.why: "You can say, 'Lovely day, isn't it?'"

items.q: Why does Emily say "no personal questions"?
options: Because money, age and salary are not polite in small talk
items.why: Inferência: ela liga "no personal questions" a dinheiro, idade e salário — não é educado ali.

items.q: How would you describe Emily's tone?
items.why: Inferência: ela dá dicas, sorri e diz "You will be fine" — é acolhedora.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We had some small talk before the meeting." Small talk is…
items.why: Small talk = bate-papo leve, conversa amigável antes do assunto sério.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Nice ___ today — the sun is out and it is warm."
items.why: Weather = clima/tempo; combina com sol e calor.

items.q: "A joke helped to break the ice." To break the ice means to…
options: make people feel relaxed and start talking
items.why: Break the ice = quebrar o gelo, deixar as pessoas à vontade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ was terrible this morning, so I was late."
items.why: Traffic = trânsito; explica o atraso.

items.q: A safe topic is…
options: a subject that is easy and polite to talk about
items.why: Safe topic = assunto seguro, fácil e educado, como o clima.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's break the ice before we start." This means to…
options: make the first talk easy and friendly
items.why: Break the ice = quebrar o gelo, começar de forma amigável.

items.q: "Come on, join in the chat!" To join in means to…
items.why: Join in = participar, entrar na conversa.

items.q: "Before the meeting, we always catch up." To catch up means to…
options: talk about recent news with someone
items.why: Catch up = colocar a conversa em dia, contar as novidades.

items.q: "He is easy to get on with." To get on with someone means to…
items.why: Get on with = dar-se bem com alguém.

items.q: "She likes to chat about the weekend." To chat about means to…
options: talk in a light, friendly way about
items.why: Chat about = conversar de forma leve sobre um assunto.
